DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## Verdict

The trial design is good, and the price arithmetic is correct. But the recommendation reverses once the trial results are read properly:

1. **ParcelLine failed two of the four stated requirements.** It delivered 93.1% on time, below the 95% minimum, and damaged 0.9% of parcels, above the 0.5% maximum.
2. **Once damage and loss are costed at the document's own £48 per incident, ParcelLine is the most expensive carrier,** at about £90,000 a year more than SwiftDrop.
3. **ParcelLine's lower customer-contact rate can't be credited to its tracking app.** Its parcels were also the only ones carrying the new proactive delivery-day text for half the trial.

On the paper's own data, **SwiftDrop** is the strongest choice. It meets every requirement, has the lowest total cost, offers a 12-month term, and has handled peak volumes for similar retailers.

## What's right

- **The trial design is sound.** Random allocation by the warehouse system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier, and measured outcomes make this a fair head-to-head comparison.
- **The cost arithmetic is correct.** The weighted prices of £3.55, £3.48 and £3.63 per parcel are right, as are the monthly totals and the £35,280 and £75,600 annual differences.
- **The paper names its own requirements and states the £48 cost per incident.** Both make the correct comparison possible.

## 1. ParcelLine doesn't meet the requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

Section 3, the Recommendation and your covering note all say all three carriers cleared the 95% threshold. Table 1 shows ParcelLine did not, and the damage requirement isn't mentioned again after section 2.

These gaps are not likely to be noise. With about 5,000 parcels each, the margin of error on the on-time rate is roughly ±0.7 percentage points, so ParcelLine's shortfall of nearly two points is real. Its 0.9% damage rate means about 45 damaged parcels, against about 20 for SwiftDrop.

## 2. With damage and loss included, ParcelLine costs the most

The document counts each damaged or lost parcel at £48, but leaves this out of the cost comparison. Adding it, plus "where is my order?" (WISMO) contacts at £3.20 each, all at 42,000 parcels a month:

| Monthly | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery charges | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damage and loss (rate × 42,000 × £48) | £8,670 | £19,760 | £6,450 |
| WISMO contacts | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total** | **£159,250** | **£166,730** | **£160,260** |
| **Annual difference vs SwiftDrop** | — | **+£89,700** | +£12,100 |

ParcelLine's £2,940 a month saving on delivery charges is outweighed by about £11,100 a month of extra damage and loss. This still leaves out the one-star reviews the paper itself identifies as the main consequence of damage.

Loss counts are small, about 4 parcels for ParcelLine and 1–2 for the others over 5,000 parcels. Most of the gap comes from damage, which is better measured.

## 3. The tracking-app explanation is confounded

From 1 May, only ParcelLine's parcels carried the new proactive delivery-day text (section 5). That text is designed to reduce exactly the "where is my order?" contacts being measured. ParcelLine also had the *worst* on-time rate, which would normally generate more such contacts, not fewer. The text message is at least as likely an explanation as the app.

This matters for two reasons:
- **The saving may come with the text, not the carrier.** If the text is rolled out across all carriers, as planned, much of ParcelLine's advantage may disappear.
- **Even taken at face value, the saving is small.** About £670 a month compared with SwiftDrop, or £540 compared with Meridian, set against £11,000 or more of extra damage cost.

The contact rates for April and May separately would show the effect directly.

## 4. Peak-season risk falls on ParcelLine

- **Trial timing.** The trial ran in April and May, outside peak season.
- **Reference fit.** ParcelLine's references are mainly fashion retailers with light parcels. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers like Larkspur.
- **Heavier, fragile items.** 30% of Larkspur's parcels are 2–10 kg lamps, mirrors and small furniture, the items most likely to be damaged.

A breakdown of damage by weight band would show whether ParcelLine's problem is concentrated in these heavier parcels.

## Smaller points

- **"Saving up to £76,000 a year"** is the comparison with the most expensive alternative. Against SwiftDrop, even on delivery charges alone, the saving was £35,000.
- **Contract terms.** The 12-month term is an advantage SwiftDrop shares, so it doesn't favour ParcelLine. Meridian's 24-month term is a genuine drawback, but small next to its strong performance.

## Suggested recommendation

> Award the standard parcel contract to **SwiftDrop** for 12 months from 1 October 2026. SwiftDrop met all four requirements in the trial and has the lowest total cost once damage, loss and customer contacts are included. It has handled peak volumes for comparable retailers. Meridian performed slightly better on service but costs about £12,000 a year more and requires a 24-month term. ParcelLine had the lowest delivery prices but did not meet the on-time or damage requirements, and its higher damage costs outweigh the price saving.

If the price gap matters, SwiftDrop's quote could be negotiated against ParcelLine's, but that negotiation should start from SwiftDrop.
